MAJOR: Prior NIT dispositioned ACTIONED but the diff adds no test for the new `enforce_from missing` config guard, nor for main-vs-`evaluate` parity / the empty-item-id `": item not found: "` formatting path; claimed coverage is not delivered.

The `enforce_from missing/invalid` guard is applied only inside `main()`'s `--all` branch; Gate 1, Gate 2 and merge-gate direct callers of `evaluate()` still lack the one-time config validation, so a missing/invalid `enforce_from` makes `should_enforce` silently return False (fail-open) on those paths unless `_date_problems` happens to catch it first.
No single-item (`--item`) path in `main()` runs the new config validation, so `enforce_from` defects surface inconsistently depending on invocation mode — observability and gate consistency gap.

With no interpreter-pin or test asserting date-only inputs, a runtime upgrade could silently shift acceptance semantics.

The added test only covers one malformed value (`2026-10-05T25`); whitespace-suffixed / extra-segment values that motivated the original blocker are untested, so regression coverage is thinner than the fix's intent.
NIT: `_date_problems` labels values as `created_at`/`enforce_from` even when the value originates from the config, mixing item-scoped and config-scoped diagnostics in one problem list.
SUMMARY: The unified `_parse_date` plus the test through `evaluate()` close the original fail-open blocker and remove the duplicated date contract — good direction.

Residual risk: config validation is scoped to the `--all` CLI path only, leaving gate/merge direct callers and `--item` invocations without the guard, and the "ACTIONED" coverage claim for the missing-`enforce_from`/parity tests is not backed by the diff.
Recommend landing the missing tests and hoisting config validation to a gate-scope check before considering this complete.
